editor_note: All five rewritten entries (9, 44, 67, 68, 69) say what the English says, so nothing here would mislead a learner. The error codes 4710 and 4712, the value mapping off/weak/medium/strong to 0–3 with default 3, the before/after transpilation split and the bitstring variable_mapping are all carried over correctly. Three things are worth fixing. First, entries 44 and 68 call solutions 해/최적해, while the rest of the page uses 솔루션 (entries 13, 20, 43, 52), so the term is inconsistent within the file. Second, entry 44 renders "best solutions found" as 최적해, which leans toward "proven optimal". Third, all five entries use the 합니다/했습니다 style instead of the house 해요체, and entry 67 calques "flat dictionary" as 평면 딕셔너리.

examples.source: contains all degenerate best solutions found
examples.suggested: 발견된 최선의 솔루션(축퇴된 해 포함)이 모두 … 들어 있어요
examples.why: The rest of the page uses 솔루션 for 'solution' (entries 13, 20, 43, 52), but here and in entry 68 it is 해/최적해. Also, 최적해 hints at a proven optimum, while the English says 'best found'.

examples.source: instead of a single flat dictionary of averaged gate counts
examples.translation: 평균 게이트 수를 담은 단일 평면 딕셔너리 대신
examples.suggested: 평균 게이트 수를 담은 중첩 없는 단일 딕셔너리 대신
examples.why: 평면 딕셔너리 is a literal calque of 'flat dictionary'. A Korean developer would say 중첩 없는 or 1단계 딕셔너리.

examples.source: The function solves discrete problems only.
examples.translation: 이 함수는 이산 문제만 풀 수 있습니다.
examples.suggested: 이 함수는 이산 문제만 풀 수 있어요.
examples.why: The rewritten entries (9, 44, 67, 68, 69) all use 합니다체 instead of the house 해요체 that appears in entries 7, 17, 18 and 20. This is a minor formal-register slip.

editor_note: Entry 28 keeps the English meaning, so a learner would not be misled. The causal clause (one QAOA round with CPU-optimized parameters, so QPU time is minimal and almost constant) and the back-reference to the description section are both intact. Two phrases still read like translated English. "인스턴스 이름은 ... 해당 예제에 대한 것입니다" copies the structure of "names are for corresponding examples". "QPU 시간은 최소한이며" uses the noun 최소한 as if it were the adjective "minimal", where a native writer would say "매우 짧고".

examples.source: Instance names are for corresponding examples in the [QOBLIB](...) problem library.
examples.translation: 인스턴스 이름은 [QOBLIB](...) 문제 라이브러리의 해당 예제에 대한 것입니다.
examples.suggested: 인스턴스 이름은 [QOBLIB](...) 문제 라이브러리의 해당 예제 이름을 따릅니다.
examples.why: '~에 대한 것입니다' copies the English 'are for' structure word for word. Saying the names follow the library's example names reads more naturally.

examples.source: the QPU time is minimal and almost constant
examples.suggested: QPU 시간은 매우 짧고 거의 일정합니다
examples.why: 최소한 is a noun meaning 'the minimum' and sounds awkward used as an adjective here. '매우 짧고' says 'minimal runtime' more naturally.

editor_note: The rewritten entries 40, 41 and 44 keep their meaning: the 10% threshold at width 9 (10 qubits), Orbit near 80–90%, about 15% near width 60, N = 50 (51 qubits) and the calibration caveat all come through intact. The problem is that their wording no longer matches the rest of the page. They use '비트스트링' where the page uses '비트열' (entries 25, 46, 65 and the table), '원시(raw)' where the page keeps bare 'raw' (38, 39, 50-52), and '보정' for calibration where entries 12 and 22 use '교정'. The last clause of 41, '표시된 가장 큰 크기에서 약 15%입니다', is also clipped and reads awkwardly.

examples.source: as the hidden-bitstring width grows ... raw success probability
examples.translation: 숨겨진 비트스트링의 폭이 커져도 ... 원시(raw) 실행 ... 원시 성공 확률
examples.suggested: 숨겨진 비트열의 폭이 커져도 ... raw 실행 ... raw 성공 확률
examples.why: The rest of the file uses '비트열' and keeps 'raw' in English, so the rewritten entries should match.

examples.source: Exact results depend on the backend calibration
examples.translation: 정확한 결과는 백엔드 보정, 회로, 실행 설정에 따라 달라집니다.
examples.suggested: 정확한 결과는 백엔드 교정 상태, 회로, 실행 설정에 따라 달라집니다.

examples.source: including approximately 15% at the largest size shown
examples.suggested: 표시된 가장 큰 크기에서도 약 15%의 성공 확률을 기록합니다.
examples.why: The clause has no clear subject or verb, so it reads awkwardly.

examples.source: one fixed hidden-bitstring width ... comparing raw execution
examples.translation: 숨겨진 비트스트링 폭을 ... 원시 실행과 Orbit 기본값을 비교한
examples.suggested: 숨겨진 비트열 폭을 ... raw 실행과 Orbit 기본값을 비교한
examples.why: Same mismatch with the rest of the page ('비트열', 'raw').

editor_note: Both rewritten entries keep the meaning. Entry 72 correctly makes Q the CNOT control and Alice's qubit the target, then applies Hadamard to Q. Entry 73's math is unchanged, and its one prose line ("A와 Q는 같은 위치에 있으므로 … 측정 결과에 따라 묶어 보겠습니다") is accurate. The only slip is in entry 72, which renders "target" as "타겟 Qubit". The rest of the page uses "목표" ("목표(target) qubit" in entry 42, "목표 큐비트" in entry 64), so entry 72 should use "목표" too.

examples.source: a CNOT gate with Q as the control and her own qubit as the target
examples.translation: Q를 제어 Qubit로, 자신의 Qubit를 타겟 Qubit로 하는 CNOT Gate를 적용한 다음
examples.suggested: Q를 제어 Qubit로, 자신의 Qubit를 목표 Qubit로 하는 CNOT Gate를 적용한 다음
examples.why: Everywhere else on the page (entries 42, 44, 64) 'target' is rendered as 목표. Using 타겟 only here breaks within-file consistency. The meaning is still clear, so this is minor.

editor_note: None of the three rewritten entries would mislead a learner. Entry 53 (seed_transpiler → "옵션을 고정하세요") and entry 87 (the Recommendations admonition, with "해의 품질과 실행 시간에 미치는 영향을 평가해 보세요") are faithful, and their terminology matches the rest of the page. There is one wording problem, in entry 78. "변수 이름으로 접근하는 첫 번째 해만 고려합니다" makes the English side remark "addressed by variable name" into a defining clause on "the first solution". It can read as "the first of the solutions accessed by name" when it should mean "only the first solution is used, and its values are read by variable name". Splitting the clause would fix it. The rest of entry 78 is accurate: "축퇴된(degenerate) 최적해" is right, and so is the variable_mapping explanation.

examples.source: Only the first solution is considered here, addressed by variable name.
examples.translation: 여기서는 변수 이름으로 접근하는 첫 번째 해만 고려합니다.
examples.suggested: 여기서는 첫 번째 해만 사용하며, 각 값은 변수 이름으로 접근합니다.
examples.why: The Korean makes the English side remark into a defining clause on 'the first solution'. It can read as 'the first among the solutions accessed by name' rather than 'use the first solution and read its values by variable name'. This is not misleading enough to fail, but a native editor would split the clause.

editor_note: Entry 60 is faithful and reads naturally. "Quantum Elements의 Qiskit Function인 Orbit으로 QFT 프로세스 충실도 벤치마킹하기" keeps Orbit's attribution to Quantum Elements, keeps "Qiskit Function" in English per house style, and renders "process fidelity" correctly as 프로세스 충실도.

The meaning of rewritten entry 12 is accurate. It uses the standard physics term 좌절(frustration), keeps the "randomly distributed between positive and negative values" claim, and keeps the triangular-arrangement example. Nothing in it would mislead a learner. One phrase reads as a calque: "이러한 좌절이 전역적으로 복합되어" renders "compounded" as 복합되다, which in Korean means "combined" rather than "amplified/accumulated". The two "…으로 이어집니다" endings in a row also feel a little mechanical. A native editor would rephrase it as something like "시스템 전체에 걸쳐 누적되어".

examples.source: this frustration is compounded globally, leading to a web of conflicting constraints.
examples.translation: 이러한 좌절이 전역적으로 복합되어 상충하는 제약 조건들의 그물망으로 이어집니다.
examples.suggested: 이러한 좌절이 시스템 전체에 걸쳐 누적되어, 서로 상충하는 제약 조건들이 얽힌 그물망을 이룹니다.
examples.why: 복합되다 means 'to be combined', not 'to be compounded/intensified'. It is a calque of 'compounded', and the sentence repeats the '…으로 이어집니다' ending from the previous sentence.

editor_note: None of the 23 rewritten entries would mislead a learner. The meaning matches the English in all of them, including the O(n^2) vs O(n) argument in [17], the 60/300-PUB arithmetic in [49], the advice in [32]/[67] to reduce N_VALUES or M or increase NUM_BATCH_PARTITIONS, and the MEM-adjusted vs raw counts caveat in [51]. Three small polish items remain. Entry [17] renders "noisy" as 잡음이 있는, but the unchanged [14] uses 노이즈가 있는. Entry [56] keeps an English semicolon between two Korean clauses. Entry [33] adds an unnecessary parenthetical gloss, 트랜스파일러(Transpiler), which no other entry on the page uses.

examples.source: the basic competition is thus between $O(n^2)$ noisy unitary gates and $O(n)$ noisy mid-circuit measurements
examples.translation: $O(n^2)$개의 잡음이 있는 유니터리 게이트와 $O(n)$개의 잡음이 있는 회로 중간 측정
examples.suggested: $O(n^2)$개의 노이즈가 있는 유니터리 게이트와 $O(n)$개의 노이즈가 있는 회로 중간 측정
examples.why: Entry [14] on the same page uses 노이즈가 있는 for 'noisy'. Using one rendering throughout keeps the page consistent.

examples.source: `dynamic/raw` and `dynamic/orbit` share a physical layout at each size; `unitary/raw` uses the transpiler's layout and routing.
examples.translation: ...물리적 레이아웃을 공유합니다; `unitary/raw`는 트랜스파일러의 레이아웃과 라우팅을 사용합니다.
examples.suggested: ...물리적 레이아웃을 공유하고, `unitary/raw`는 트랜스파일러의 레이아웃과 라우팅을 사용합니다.
examples.why: Korean prose does not join sentences with a semicolon. This reads as a calque of the English punctuation.

examples.source: `OPTIMIZATION_LEVEL=0` asks Qiskit's transpiler to do the required translation and routing with minimal optimization.
examples.translation: `OPTIMIZATION_LEVEL=0`은 Qiskit의 트랜스파일러(Transpiler)에게 최소한의 최적화로 필요한 변환과 라우팅만 수행하도록 요청합니다.
examples.suggested: `OPTIMIZATION_LEVEL=0`은 Qiskit 트랜스파일러가 최적화를 최소한으로 하면서 필요한 변환과 라우팅을 수행하도록 합니다.
examples.why: The (Transpiler) gloss appears in no other entry on the page, where the word is always plain 트랜스파일러. The phrasing is also stiff.
